title: Chapters 1 & 2 — Teacher Quiz
instructions: Answer all questions. Show all working for conversions and calculations. Calculators are not permitted. Mark yourself using your own reference: no official mark scheme is supplied.

questions.text:
**Original question 1(a)**

Convert the binary number 11010110 to denary.

**Original question 1(b)**

Convert denary 173 to hexadecimal.

**Original question 2(a)**

Represent denary -53 as an 8-bit two's complement binary number. Show your working.

**Original question 2(b)**

The 8-bit binary number 11010110 is stored using two's complement. Convert it to denary.

**Original question 3(a)**

Write denary 507 using Binary Coded Decimal (BCD).

**Original question 3(b)**

State one difference between ASCII and UTF-8 Unicode.

**Original question 4(a)**

Calculate the minimum storage required for the pixel data. Give your answer in bytes and KiB. Show your working.

**Source limitation:** The original image specifications are not shown in the supplied question screenshot.

**Original question 4(b)**

State one advantage of storing a graphic as a vector graphic when the image needs to be enlarged.

**Original question 5(a)**

Define sampling rate.

**Original question 5(b)**

State the requirement given by Nyquist's theorem when choosing a sampling rate.

**Original question 5(c)**

State one difference between lossless compression and lossy compression.

**Original question 6**

A program is required to convert a denary integer into an 8-bit binary number. The program must: input an integer Number; check that Number is between 0 and 255 inclusive; output "Invalid input" if the value is outside this range; otherwise convert the number to an 8-bit binary representation; use DIV and MOD; not use a built-in binary conversion function. Write pseudocode to perform this task.

**Original question 7(a)**

State two differences between a LAN and a WAN.

**Original question 7(b)**

State one difference between a thin client and a thick client.

**Original question 8(a)**

Name this network topology.

**Source limitation:** The original topology diagram is not shown in the supplied question screenshot.

**Original question 8(b)**

**Original question 8(c)**

State one disadvantage of using this topology.

**Source limitation:** The referenced topology diagram is not shown in the supplied question screenshot.

**Original question 9**

Fibre-optic cable is being considered instead of twisted-pair cable. State: (i) one advantage of fibre-optic cable (ii) one disadvantage of fibre-optic cable.

**Original question 10(a)**

State the purpose of an Internet Service Provider (ISP).

**Original question 10(b)**

State the purpose of an Internet Exchange Point (IXP).

**Original question 10(c)**

Explain the function of a router in the Internet infrastructure.

**Original question 11(a)**

Convert the following IPv4 binary address to dotted decimal notation: 11000000 10101000 00000001 00011110

**Original question 11(b)**

Explain the purpose of Network Address Translation (NAT).

State the purpose of the Domain Name System (DNS).
